calls.reason: Candidate 38 passes with its current geometry. Hole 1 is a dry 321-yard split-fairway par 4. The tree-lined division gives the tee shot a placement choice, though its exceptionally broad fairway and 9/9 safe dispersion make this the forgiving setup hole. Hole 2 is a 229-yard long par 3 with water left and forward of the target and greenside bunkers; the 3-wood demand makes it a substantial target test, while all nine dispersion samples remain playable. Hole 3 is a dry 439-yard dogleg-left par 4 with water to the right/front of play. The turn and hazard give the tee shot consequence, and 7/9 safe samples indicate a challenge with alternatives. The par-4/3/4 sequence and contrast between a broad placement hole, a long water-influenced target, and a turning finish provide good variety, even though the two par 4s temper it. Recent rounds feature many doglegs and water, but this set’s long par 3 between a generous split fairway and a water-side dogleg gives it sufficient freshness. The easy opener is balanced by the demanding par 3 and longer, turning par 4; the dispersion evidence supports recoverable difficulty rather than an exact-shot trap. Geometry facts confirm water on holes 2 and 3, and none on hole 1.

The mapped course layout, hazards, tees, and greens are well preserved, and the greens read as single natural putting surfaces. The broad Hole 1 and bent Hole 3 fairways show checkerboard-like crosshatching rather than clear, smoothly fanning transverse mowing bands.

issues.consequence: At overview scale, the fairway will read as tiled or crosshatched turf rather than striped mowing.

issues.detail: The bent fairway has a fixed checkerboard-like pattern instead of bands that rotate and fan with the curve.
issues.consequence: The mowing pattern will visually conflict with the fairway's changing direction and make it read as a grid.
